title: Mortgage Calculator
description: Estimate principal-and-interest payments from the financed balance, fixed rate and loan term. Add taxes, insurance and association charges separately when comparing with a lender quote.

title: Loan Calculator
description: See how a fixed-rate installment loan turns principal, APR and term into a regular payment and total interest cost.

title: Auto Loan Calculator
description: Estimate a vehicle loan after the down payment or trade-in has already been reflected in the amount financed. Taxes, dealer fees and optional products belong in that balance if they are financed.

title: Interest Calculator
description: Project how an amount changes under a stated annual rate and compounding assumption. This version compounds once per year and leaves fees and taxes out.

title: Payment Calculator
description: Find the level monthly payment needed to repay a fixed-rate balance by the end of the chosen term. It models regular end-of-month payments.

title: Retirement Calculator
description: Project a retirement balance from current savings, monthly additions and an assumed steady return. The estimate is nominal and does not account for inflation or investment volatility.

title: Amortization Calculator
description: Calculate the scheduled monthly payment and show how much of the first payment is interest versus principal. A full schedule can be derived by repeating that balance update.

title: Investment Calculator
description: Estimate the ending value of an initial portfolio plus monthly investing under a constant annual return. Contributions are assumed to arrive at month end.

title: Currency Calculator
description: Convert an amount using an exchange rate you provide, then optionally deduct a percentage conversion fee. Rates move continuously and are not fetched live.

title: Inflation Calculator
description: Translate a present amount into its future purchasing-power equivalent using your own annual inflation assumption. This is a scenario, not an official price index lookup.

title: Finance Calculator
description: Discount a level annual cash flow to its present value and compare it with the upfront investment. This helps screen a simple project before detailed cash-flow modeling.

title: Mortgage Payoff Calculator
description: Compare a standard loan payment with an added monthly principal amount to estimate an earlier payoff and interest savings.

title: Income Tax Calculator
description: Apply a user-entered effective tax rate to taxable income after a deduction. It is a planning estimate, not a current jurisdiction-specific tax return calculation.

title: Compound Interest Calculator
description: Model compounding alongside regular monthly contributions so you can separate the starting principal from new deposits. The assumed return stays constant.

title: Salary Calculator
description: Convert annual income to an approximate after-tax annual amount using a deduction and one effective-rate assumption. Pay frequency and benefits are not modeled.

title: 401K Calculator
description: Project a workplace retirement account from its current balance and monthly deposits. Enter the combined employee and employer deposits in the contribution field.

title: Interest Rate Calculator
description: Infer the annualized compound growth rate between an initial amount and an ending amount over a known holding period.

title: Sales Tax Calculator
description: Add a chosen sales-tax rate to a pre-tax price and separate the tax portion from the amount paid. Enter the local combined rate yourself.

title: House Affordability Calculator
description: Estimate a home-price ceiling from gross monthly income, other debt, an assumed housing-and-debt share and loan terms. Set the share to match the screening rule you want to test; lenders may use different limits.

title: Savings Calculator
description: Forecast a savings balance when you add the same amount each month and earn a stated annual rate. It assumes monthly compounding and end-of-month deposits.

title: Rent Calculator
description: Check how rent fits a monthly budget after fixed bills, variable spending and a savings target. The remaining amount is a cash-flow ceiling, not a market rent recommendation.

title: Marriage Tax Calculator
description: Compare a combined-income scenario under one assumed effective tax rate. Actual marriage effects depend on filing status, deductions, credits and jurisdiction.

title: Estate Tax Calculator
description: Estimate tax on an estate value above a user-entered exemption using a flat assumed rate. Exemption, gifts, deductions and state rules must be set for the applicable year.

title: Pension Calculator
description: Estimate the fixed monthly income that a pension fund could support for a chosen payout period and return. It does not reproduce a specific plan’s benefit formula or survivor options.

title: Social Security Calculator
description: Project cumulative retirement benefits from the monthly estimate on your Social Security statement, a benefit duration and an assumed cost-of-living adjustment. It does not calculate eligibility or your benefit record.

title: Annuity Calculator
description: Calculate the monthly deposit required to build a target annuity balance over a fixed saving period at an assumed rate.

title: Annuity Payout Calculator
description: Convert an annuity balance into level monthly withdrawals over a chosen finite term. A lifetime payout requires insurer pricing and mortality assumptions.

title: Credit Card Calculator
description: Estimate the time needed to clear revolving card debt when you keep paying a fixed monthly amount and stop adding new charges.

title: Credit Cards Payoff Calculator
description: Estimate payoff timing and interest for a card balance at a stated APR and fixed monthly payment, assuming no new purchases or fees.

title: Debt Payoff Calculator
description: Estimate repayment time for one debt under a fixed monthly payment. For several balances, calculate each separately or use the consolidation comparison.

title: Debt Consolidation Calculator
description: Compare a new fixed-rate consolidation offer with the current APR across the same payoff window, including the stated fee.

title: Repayment Calculator
description: Calculate the monthly amount that fully repays a fixed-rate debt within the selected time.

title: Student Loan Calculator
description: Estimate a fixed-payment student loan under an entered rate and term. Income-driven plans, deferment, subsidies and federal forgiveness rules are not included.

title: College Cost Calculator
description: Project one year of education cost forward using your assumed annual tuition increase, then extend the period to estimate a later-year bill.

title: Simple Interest Calculator
description: Calculate interest that accrues only on the original principal, with no interest-on-interest compounding. The result shows the balance at the end of the period and separates the interest earned.

title: CD Calculator
description: Estimate a certificate deposit balance at maturity using an annual rate and term. The annual compounding assumption may differ from the bank’s exact day-count and compounding schedule.

title: Bond Calculator
description: Estimate a bond’s future value under a stated annual yield and time horizon. This simplified growth estimate omits coupon timing, market price and reinvestment risk.

title: Mutual Fund Calculator
description: Project a mutual-fund investment with recurring monthly contributions and a user-supplied annual return. The result excludes expense ratios, loads and taxes unless reflected in the rate.

title: Roth IRA Calculator
description: Illustrate long-term account growth for monthly Roth IRA contributions. Contribution eligibility, annual limits and qualified withdrawal treatment depend on current tax rules and are not checked.

title: IRA Calculator
description: Project an IRA balance from the current account value and monthly contributions. Tax deductions, contribution limits and withdrawal taxes are outside this growth model.

title: RMD Calculator
description: Divide a prior year-end retirement balance by the applicable distribution divisor you enter. Confirm the correct IRS table and year because spouse and inherited-account rules can change the divisor.

title: VAT Calculator
description: Add a user-entered value-added tax rate to a net price, or read the tax component as a separate amount. Tax rates vary by place, product and date.

title: Cash Back or Low Interest Calculator
description: Compare a cash rebate with interest saved by choosing a lower financing rate over the same payoff period. Enter the actual APRs and upfront rebate to compare the dollar totals.

title: Auto Lease Calculator
description: Estimate monthly depreciation and financing charges on a lease from vehicle price, upfront cash, rate and term. A real lease also depends on residual value and fees, which this simplified purchase schema does not include.

title: Depreciation Calculator
description: Calculate straight-line depreciation and remaining book value from asset cost, salvage value and useful life. Tax depreciation can use different methods and conventions.

title: Average Return Calculator
description: Annualize the total change between two values over a holding period. This is a compound annual growth rate, not the arithmetic mean of yearly returns.

title: Margin Calculator
description: Compute gross profit and gross margin from the cost and selling price. Margin uses selling price as its denominator; markup uses cost.

title: Discount Calculator
description: Apply a percentage discount to an original price and show the savings and reduced price.

title: Business Loan Calculator
description: Estimate the fixed monthly payment and total interest for a business term loan. Origination charges, variable rates and balloon terms need separate modeling.

title: Debt Ratio Calculator
description: Use income inputs to compare annual obligations only when the second amount is repurposed as debt; this model returns a simple debt-to-income ratio.

title: Real Estate Calculator
description: Estimate mortgage payment and housing debt share for a property purchase using price, down payment and income assumptions. Ongoing ownership costs are not included.

title: Take-Home Pay Calculator
description: Estimate net annual income after a deduction and a configurable effective tax rate. For payroll planning, add all applicable taxes and deductions into your assumptions.

title: Personal Loan Calculator
description: Estimate a personal loan’s regular payment and total interest under a fixed APR and term, before lender fees.

title: Boat Loan Calculator
description: Plan the payment for a boat loan balance, annual rate and term. If taxes, delivery or accessories are financed, include them in the principal amount.

title: Lease Calculator
description: Estimate a lease-like fixed monthly financing amount from the balance, annual rate and term. For vehicle leases, residual value, mileage and fees can materially change the quote.

title: Refinance Calculator
description: Compare remaining debt payments at the current rate against a refinance offer after adding closing costs to the new balance. The selected payoff window should match the comparison horizon.

title: Budget Calculator
description: Subtract fixed expenses, variable spending and a savings goal from take-home income to find the remaining monthly amount.

title: Rental Property Calculator
description: Estimate annual rent after vacancy, operating cash flow, gross yield and cash-on-cash return for a rental property. Financing and income tax are excluded.

title: IRR Calculator
description: Approximate the internal rate of return when one initial outlay is followed by equal positive annual cash flows. Uneven cash flows need a dated cash-flow series solver.

title: ROI Calculator
description: Measure total gain relative to the original investment. This simple return excludes the timing of interim cash flows.

title: APR Calculator
description: Estimate a fee-inclusive nominal APR for a fixed-payment loan by solving the monthly cash flows after upfront lender fees. The effective annual rate is also shown for comparison; legal APR disclosures may use jurisdiction-specific rules.

title: FHA Loan Calculator
description: Estimate a fixed-rate payment with editable upfront and annual mortgage-insurance assumptions. Both insurance rates default to zero as illustrative inputs; replace them with the figures for the loan scenario you are comparing.

title: VA Mortgage Calculator
description: Estimate a fixed-rate payment after adding an editable VA funding-fee assumption to the financed balance. The fee defaults to zero for a neutral example; replace it with the applicable amount for your eligibility and transaction.

title: Home Equity Loan Calculator
description: Calculate the fixed installment for a home equity loan balance. The output excludes closing costs and does not establish how much equity a lender will approve.

title: HELOC Calculator
description: Estimate interest-only monthly carrying cost on an outstanding line balance using the entered annual rate. A variable HELOC rate can change, and this estimate does not repay principal.

title: Down Payment Calculator
description: Show the down payment as a share of the purchase price and the remaining amount to finance.

title: Rent vs Buy Calculator
description: Compare cumulative rent with estimated ownership equity after a chosen period, using home growth and rent increases you specify. Taxes, maintenance and transaction costs are omitted.

title: Payback Period Calculator
description: Estimate how many years of equal annual cash benefits are needed to recover an upfront cost, ignoring discounting.

title: Present Value Calculator
description: Discount a single future amount to today’s value with a stated annual discount rate and time period.

title: Future Value Calculator
description: Grow a present lump sum across a chosen number of years at a constant annual rate.

title: Commission Calculator
description: Calculate the gross commission on a sale and the portion allocated to you under the entered split.

title: Mortgage Calculator UK
description: Estimate monthly principal-and-interest payments from a UK mortgage balance, annual rate and term. Use the lender’s compounding and repayment conventions for an exact offer comparison.

title: Canadian Mortgage Calculator
description: Estimate a monthly mortgage payment after converting the entered nominal annual rate with semi-annual compounding into an equivalent monthly rate. Lender payment timing and mortgage insurance may still change the quoted amount.

title: Mortgage Amortization Calculator
description: Estimate monthly mortgage payment and payoff timing when you add a recurring extra principal amount. It assumes the extra amount is applied each month.

title: Percent Off Calculator
description: Find the dollar savings and final price after taking a percentage off a marked price.

title: BMI Calculator
description: Calculate adult body mass index from height and weight, then see the standard adult screening category and the weight interval that corresponds to the healthy BMI range. The calculation is intended for adults and does not measure body fat directly. BMI = weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. Categories are the CDC adult thresholds; for people under 20, interpretation requires age- and sex-specific growth charts.

title: Calorie Calculator
description: Estimate daily calorie maintenance from a resting-energy equation and an activity multiplier, then model a modest goal adjustment. This gives a planning starting point, not a measured metabolic rate or a prescribed diet. The calculator applies Mifflin–St Jeor resting energy expenditure and multiplies by the selected activity factor. The goal adjustment is user-entered and is shown separately from estimated maintenance.

title: Body Fat Calculator
description: Estimate adult body-fat percentage from BMI, age, and the sex term used in the published Deurenberg equation. Because this is inferred from height and weight rather than measured directly, treat it as a rough population equation, not a body-composition scan. Deurenberg adult estimate: body fat % = 1.20×BMI + 0.23×age − 10.8×sex − 5.4, with male=1 and female=0 in the original equation.

title: BMR Calculator
description: Estimate basal metabolic rate, the energy used at rest, from age, height, weight, and the Mifflin–St Jeor equation. Use it as an estimate of resting needs before adding daily movement or exercise. Mifflin–St Jeor: men 10W+6.25H−5A+5; women 10W+6.25H−5A−161, where W is kg, H is cm, and A is years. This estimates resting energy only; walking, work, exercise, and digestion add to total daily expenditure.

title: Macro Calculator
description: Turn a daily calorie target into grams of protein, carbohydrate, and fat using percentages that you choose. The tool checks that the three energy shares total 100%, making it useful for comparing macro plans on a consistent calorie basis. Protein and carbohydrate provide about 4 kcal per gram; fat provides about 9 kcal per gram. Each macro’s grams equal allocated calories divided by its energy-per-gram factor.

title: Ideal Weight Calculator
description: Compare four classic height-based ideal-weight equations and show their average as a reference point. These formulas were devised for clinical estimates, so the spread is more informative than treating one result as a personal target. The calculator evaluates Devine, Robinson, Miller, and Hamwi formulas using height above 5 feet, then averages their estimates. Each formula is a historical rule of thumb with a different derivation.

title: Pregnancy Calculator
description: Estimate an expected due date and gestational age from the first day of the last menstrual period, with an optional adjustment for a cycle length different from 28 days. Pregnancy dating is approximate and is commonly confirmed by ultrasound. Estimated due date = LMP + 280 days + (usual cycle length − 28 days). Gestational age is counted from the first day of the last menstrual period.

title: Pregnancy Weight Gain Calculator
description: Compare current pregnancy weight gain with widely used singleton or twin-pregnancy total ranges based on pre-pregnancy BMI. It also shows a simple progress comparison, while leaving individual targets to prenatal care. The calculator selects the CDC-posted Institute of Medicine total-gain range using pre-pregnancy BMI and pregnancy type. A linear progress line is only a visual comparison, not a clinical trimester-specific growth model.

title: Pregnancy Conception Calculator
description: Estimate a conception date from a due date or last menstrual period using conventional pregnancy dating intervals. The result is a calendar estimate because ovulation timing and cycle length vary from person to person. A typical estimate places conception about 266 days before the estimated due date, or near 14 days after a 28-day-cycle LMP.

title: Due Date Calculator
description: Estimate a pregnancy due date using the last menstrual period, conception date, or IVF transfer date. The selected dating method matters, and a healthcare professional may confirm or revise the estimate with ultrasound. LMP dating adds 280 days; conception dating adds 266 days; a day-5 embryo transfer adds 261 days. These are conventional estimates rather than a prediction of the delivery date.

title: Pace Calculator
description: Convert a running or walking distance and elapsed time into pace per kilometre or mile and average speed. The result helps compare workouts recorded in different distance units, provided the entered duration is moving time. Pace = elapsed time ÷ distance. Speed = distance ÷ elapsed time. Unit conversion uses 1 mile = 1.609344 kilometres.

title: Army Body Fat Calculator
description: Calculate waist-to-height ratio using the Army’s current body-composition screening measure and compare it with the published 0.55 standard. The tool does not estimate body-fat percentage; the Army replaced its former circumference tape test with this ratio in 2026. Waist-to-height ratio = abdominal circumference at the navel ÷ height, using the same unit for both. Current Army guidance sets a screening standard below 0.55.

title: Carbohydrate Calculator
description: Translate a chosen share of daily calories into carbohydrate grams and compare it with the adult acceptable macronutrient distribution range. The range is a population reference, not an individualized treatment plan. Carbohydrate provides about 4 kcal per gram, so grams = daily calories × carbohydrate percentage ÷ 100 ÷ 4. The adult reference range is 45–65% of calories.

title: Lean Body Mass Calculator
description: Estimate lean body mass from total weight and a body-fat percentage estimate. The result represents everything outside the estimated fat mass, including water, bone, and muscle, rather than muscle alone. Fat mass = body weight × body-fat fraction; lean body mass = body weight − fat mass. Because the input percentage is itself an estimate, any error in that percentage carries directly into the lean-mass result.

title: Healthy Weight Calculator
description: Find the adult weight interval associated with BMI 18.5 through 24.9 at a given height. The interval is a screening reference; body build, age, pregnancy, and health conditions may make BMI-based ranges less useful. For height h in metres, the weight interval is 18.5h² through 24.9h² kilograms. CDC adult BMI categories apply to adults 20 and older.

title: Calories Burned Calculator
description: Estimate calories used during a chosen activity from body weight, duration, and a MET intensity value. The MET value is an average from activity research, so the result is a comparison estimate rather than a wearable-grade measurement. Approximate gross kcal = MET × 3.5 × weight(kg) ÷ 200 × minutes. MET values are standardized activity intensities; actual energy use varies with pace and physiology.

title: One Rep Max Calculator
description: Estimate the greatest load you could lift for one repetition from a submaximal set and repetitions completed. Compare Epley and Brzycki estimates, while treating the result as a training approximation rather than a safe substitute for a tested max. Epley: 1RM = load×(1+reps/30). Brzycki: 1RM = load×36/(37−reps). Both are estimates and become less dependable at high repetition counts.

title: Target Heart Rate Calculator
description: Estimate age-predicted maximum heart rate and moderate or vigorous training zones from the simple 220-minus-age rule. These broad ranges help frame exercise intensity but cannot account for medication, fitness, or heart conditions. Estimated maximum = 220−age. Moderate zone is 50–70% and vigorous zone is 70–85% of that estimate, following American Heart Association guidance.

title: Protein Calculator
description: Estimate daily protein grams by multiplying body weight by a selected grams-per-kilogram target. The target is configurable because protein needs depend on age, activity, health, and clinical goals. Daily protein = weight in kg × selected grams of protein per kg per day. This calculator does not infer an optimal target from a medical diagnosis.

title: Fat Intake Calculator
description: Convert a chosen percentage of daily calories from fat into grams and show the corresponding calorie amount. This keeps the energy conversion transparent while allowing the user to select a target for comparison. Fat provides about 9 kcal per gram, so fat grams = daily calories × selected percentage ÷ 100 ÷ 9. The percentage refers to energy share, not weight share; the calculation reports total fat and does not split fatty-acid types.

title: TDEE Calculator
description: Estimate total daily energy expenditure by multiplying Mifflin–St Jeor resting energy expenditure by an activity factor. Separating the resting estimate from the activity multiplier makes assumptions visible when using the result for planning. TDEE ≈ Mifflin–St Jeor REE × activity factor. Common planning factors range from 1.2 for sedentary to 1.9 for very high activity.

title: Ovulation Calculator
description: Estimate a likely ovulation date and fertile window from the first day of the last period and usual cycle length. Calendar estimates cannot confirm ovulation, especially with irregular cycles. A common estimate places ovulation about 14 days before the next period; the fertile window is approximated as five days before through one day after ovulation.

title: Conception Calculator
description: Estimate a likely conception window from the last menstrual period and typical cycle length, or work backward from an estimated due date. This is approximate calendar arithmetic and cannot establish the exact date of fertilization. The estimate places ovulation about 14 days before the next expected period; conception is most likely around ovulation, with a wider possible window because sperm can remain viable for several days.

title: Period Calculator
description: Project the next expected period, likely ovulation, and a broad fertile window from the last period and average cycle length. Use it as a cycle-planning aid, not as contraception or a diagnosis of cycle irregularity. Next period = LMP + cycle length. Estimated ovulation is about 14 days before that date; the fertile window is approximated from five days before to one day after ovulation.

title: GFR Calculator
description: Estimate adult kidney filtration using the 2021 race-free CKD-EPI creatinine equation and a standardized serum creatinine result. eGFR is a screening estimate that clinicians interpret with urine albumin, trends, and other findings. 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation: 142×min(Scr/κ,1)^α×max(Scr/κ,1)^−1.200×0.9938^age×1.012 if female; κ and α depend on sex term.

title: Body Type Calculator
description: Classify a clothing-fit silhouette from bust, waist, and hip measurements using transparent ratio rules. The output is a descriptive shape label for garment-fit exploration, not a health or personality category. The comparison uses bust-to-hip and waist-to-bust/hip proportions with a small tolerance band to identify balanced, pear, inverted-triangle, or straighter silhouettes.

title: Body Surface Area Calculator
description: Estimate body surface area from height and weight with the Mosteller equation. BSA is a derived measurement used in some clinical calculations, but medication dosing must follow the prescriber’s method and patient-specific guidance. Mosteller BSA = √[height(cm)×weight(kg)/3600] square metres. This compact empirical equation estimates a surface-area index from two measurements; it does not model body shape and should not be substituted into a dose calculation without clinician direction.

title: BAC Calculator
description: Produce a rough Widmark-style blood alcohol concentration estimate from alcohol amount, body weight, distribution factor, and elapsed time. The result is highly uncertain and must never be used to decide whether driving or operating equipment is safe. Estimated BAC% ≈ alcohol grams ÷ (r×body weight grams) × 100 − 0.015×hours, floored at zero. Absorption, drink size, food, and metabolism vary widely.

title: Anorexic BMI Calculator
description: Calculate BMI and show how it compares with standard adult thresholds, including the very low BMI range below 16. The historical title is retained for search, but BMI cannot diagnose anorexia nervosa or determine someone’s nutritional status by itself. BMI=weight(kg)/height(m)². Adult BMI under 16 is a very low screening value; eating-disorder diagnosis depends on clinical assessment, not a BMI threshold alone.

title: Weight Watchers Points Calculator
description: Estimate a single food serving with a clearly labeled historical classic Points formula, or switch to a simple daily budget tracker. The food estimate uses calories, total fat, and dietary fiber from a label, making it useful for historical recipe comparisons rather than current plan tracking. The historical formula in U.S. Patent 6,040,531 is calories/50 + total fat grams/12 − dietary fiber grams/5, with the result rounded to the nearest half point. This old formula is not the current proprietary WeightWatchers Points algorithm; modern programs use different nutrition factors and personalized rules.

title: Overweight Calculator
description: Compare adult BMI with the standard BMI 25 screening threshold and estimate the weight corresponding to that threshold for a given height. The output is a screening comparison and does not judge body composition or an individual’s health. BMI=weight(kg)/height(m)². The BMI-25 comparison weight is 25×height(m)²; the difference is shown only when current weight is above that reference. This is a screening threshold for adults, not a health boundary; muscularity, body composition, age, and clinical context all affect interpretation.

title: Scientific Calculator
description: Evaluate a mathematical expression with standard operator precedence, powers, roots, trigonometric functions, logarithms, and constants. This scientific calculator is useful for homework checks and engineering estimates when the expression is within JavaScript number precision. Enter a concise expression using +, -, *, /, ^, parentheses, sqrt(), sin(), cos(), tan(), log(), ln(), abs(), pi, or e. Trigonometric functions use radians; exponentiation binds before multiplication.

title: Fraction Calculator
description: Add, subtract, multiply, or divide two signed fractions and return a reduced numerator and denominator. The result includes the decimal value so you can compare a fraction with a measurement or another representation. Fractions are normalized by a greatest-common-divisor reduction. Addition and subtraction use a common denominator; multiplication multiplies corresponding terms; division multiplies by the reciprocal.

title: Percentage Calculator
description: Solve the three common percentage questions: find a percentage of a number, determine what percent one amount is of another, or find the percentage change between two values. Each mode uses a clearly defined base to avoid confusing percentage points with percent change. Choose the relationship you know. “P% of X” is X × P/100; “A is what percent of B” is A/B × 100; percent change is (new − old)/|old| × 100.

title: Triangle Calculator
description: Find a triangle’s third side and area from two sides and their included angle. The calculator checks the angle and side lengths before applying the included-angle area relation and the cosine rule. With sides a and b and included angle C, area = ab sin(C)/2 and c = √(a²+b²−2ab cos(C)). The entered angle is in degrees.

title: Volume Calculator
description: Calculate volume for a cube, rectangular prism, cylinder, sphere, cone, or triangular prism. Select a shape and enter only its defining dimensions to get a result in cubic units. The selected solid uses its standard geometric volume rule: for example cylinder πr²h, sphere 4πr³/3, cone πr²h/3, or prism base area multiplied by length.

title: Standard Deviation Calculator
description: Measure the spread of a numeric dataset with either population or sample standard deviation. The output also reports mean and variance so you can see both the dataset’s center and the squared spread used in the calculation. Population deviation divides the sum of squared deviations from the mean by n. Sample deviation divides by n−1, applying Bessel’s correction when the list represents a sample.

title: Random Number Generator
description: Generate a batch of random numbers within a range you choose, using integer or decimal mode and a bounded quantity. Integer draws use cryptographically secure rejection sampling for a uniform inclusive range, making the results suitable for general random selection and software testing. Integer mode samples from every whole number between the entered minimum and maximum, including both endpoints; rejection sampling avoids modulo bias. Decimal mode uses secure random bits to produce values from the minimum up to, but not including, the maximum. The browser or runtime must provide the Web Crypto random generator.

title: Number Sequence Calculator
description: Inspect an ordered list for a constant arithmetic difference or constant geometric ratio, then extend the sequence by one term. It also reports the observed step pattern so a simple sequence can be checked without guessing its rule. For an arithmetic sequence, the next term is last + d where d is the repeated difference. For a geometric sequence, it is last × r where r is the repeated ratio.

title: Percent Error Calculator
description: Compare an observed measurement with an accepted reference and express the absolute discrepancy as a percentage of the reference. Signed error and absolute error are shown separately, which helps distinguish direction from magnitude. Signed percent error = (observed − reference)/reference × 100. Absolute percent error uses the absolute value of that signed percentage.

title: Exponent Calculator
description: Raise a real base to a real exponent and inspect the power, including common integer, fractional, and negative powers. The validation catches undefined real-number cases such as zero to a negative exponent or a negative base with a non-integer exponent. For a nonzero base, a negative exponent means the reciprocal of the corresponding positive power: a^(−n)=1/a^n. Fractional exponents are evaluated over real numbers only when the result is real.

title: Binary Calculator
description: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division on two binary integers and show the result in base 2 and base 10. Inputs are parsed as bit strings, so leading zeros are allowed and do not change the represented value. Each binary string is converted to an integer, the selected arithmetic operation is applied, and the result is converted back to base 2. Division is integer quotient with remainder.

title: Hex Calculator
description: Add, subtract, multiply, or divide two hexadecimal integers using digits 0–9 and A–F. Results are returned in hexadecimal and decimal, making it easier to verify address arithmetic, bit-level examples, and number-system conversions. The operands are parsed in base 16, the chosen integer operation is performed, and the result is converted back to uppercase hexadecimal. Division returns an integer quotient and remainder.

title: Half-Life Calculator
description: Estimate the remaining quantity of a decaying substance after a specified number of half-lives. Enter the initial amount, half-life duration, and elapsed time to see the remaining quantity and fraction left under an ideal exponential-decay model. Remaining amount = initial amount × (1/2)^(elapsed time / half-life). This continuous model works for any nonnegative elapsed duration; it does not predict individual decay events.

title: Quadratic Formula Calculator
description: Solve a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, reporting real roots or a complex conjugate pair and the discriminant. This makes the sign of the discriminant visible alongside the solutions. The discriminant is D=b²−4ac and roots are (−b ± √D)/(2a). If D is negative, √D is represented as an imaginary component. When D is zero, both solutions coincide at one repeated root; the denominator 2a also explains why a cannot be zero.

title: Slope Calculator
description: Find the slope and line equation through two coordinate points. It identifies vertical lines separately because their slope is undefined, while still giving their equation. For distinct x-coordinates, slope m=(y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁), and point-slope form yields y=mx+b. When x₁=x₂, the line is vertical and has equation x=x₁.

title: Log Calculator
description: Evaluate log base b of a positive number x, answering the question b raised to what power gives x. The base is checked against the logarithm’s domain, and the change-of-base relation is shown for verification. log_b(x)=ln(x)/ln(b), requiring x>0, b>0, and b≠1. The logarithm is the inverse of exponentiation: its answer y must satisfy b^y=x. The change-of-base relation permits any valid base to be evaluated with natural logarithms.

title: Area Calculator
description: Calculate area for a rectangle, triangle, circle, or trapezoid from the dimensions each shape requires. The selected formula and squared unit keep the geometry clear, whether checking a room plan or a classroom exercise. Rectangle area is lw; triangle area is bh/2; circle area is πr²; trapezoid area is (a+b)h/2 for parallel sides a and b. For the trapezoid, h is the perpendicular distance between its parallel sides, not the sloping side. Use matching length units throughout so the result is consistently in square metres, square centimetres, or another squared unit.

title: Sample Size Calculator
description: Estimate a survey sample size for a population proportion using a confidence level, margin of error, expected proportion, and optional finite-population correction. The result is rounded up because a partial respondent cannot satisfy the requested precision. The large-population estimate is n₀=z²p(1−p)/e². For finite population N, apply n=n₀/[1+(n₀−1)/N]. The method assumes a simple random sample and a proportion outcome.

title: Probability Calculator
description: Compute a binomial probability for exactly, at most, or at least k successes in n independent trials with the same success probability. It also reports the expected number of successes, so the event probability has useful context. For X~Binomial(n,p), P(X=k)=C(n,k)p^k(1−p)^(n−k). Cumulative options sum the relevant outcomes from 0 through n. “At most k” includes zero through k; “at least k” includes k through n. The model describes a fixed number of independent trials with one shared success chance, such as repeated draws with replacement or repeated fair coin flips.

title: Statistics Calculator
description: Summarize a list of measurements with count, mean, median, mode, range, sample standard deviation, and quartiles. This broad statistics calculator is suited to a quick descriptive check before choosing a more specialized statistical method. Mean is sum/n; median is the center of the sorted values; range is max−min. Quartiles use the median-of-halves convention, excluding the overall median for odd-sized lists.

title: Mean, Median, Mode, Range Calculator
description: Find the four familiar summaries of a dataset: arithmetic mean, median, mode, and range. The sorted input and tie handling make it easy to spot outliers or repeated values before interpreting the numbers. The mean adds all observations and divides by the count; the median is the middle sorted observation (or midpoint of two middles); mode is the most frequent value; range is maximum minus minimum.

title: Permutation and Combination Calculator
description: Count ordered arrangements or unordered selections from n distinct items taken r at a time. Choose permutations when order matters and combinations when only membership matters, with integer and range checks for both counts. Permutation P(n,r)=n!/(n−r)!; combination C(n,r)=n!/[r!(n−r)!]. The calculation uses exact BigInt arithmetic before rendering the count.

title: Z-score Calculator
description: Convert an observation into standard-deviation units from a distribution’s mean. A positive z-score is above the mean, a negative score is below it, and zero is exactly at the mean. z=(x−μ)/σ, where σ is a positive population standard deviation. The result is a distance in standard-deviation units, not a probability by itself.

title: Confidence Interval Calculator
description: Build a two-sided confidence interval for a population mean from a sample mean, sample standard deviation, sample size, and confidence level. It uses Student’s t critical value, which accounts for the extra uncertainty from estimating population spread. Interval = x̄ ± t* s/√n with n−1 degrees of freedom. The t critical value is numerically evaluated from the selected confidence level.

title: Ratio Calculator
description: Reduce a two-part ratio to its simplest whole-number terms and scale it to a requested total. Decimal inputs are converted to a practical common integer scale before the greatest common factor is removed. For positive parts a:b, divide both by gcd(a,b). Given a total T, the first share is T×a/(a+b) and the second is T×b/(a+b).

title: Distance Calculator
description: Measure straight-line distance between two points in a plane or in three-dimensional coordinates. The coordinate differences and Euclidean distance are returned so the geometry behind the result remains easy to inspect. 2D distance is √[(x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²]. For 3D, add the squared z-coordinate difference under the same square root. This is the shortest straight segment between the entered coordinates, so it does not account for roads, terrain, or travel routes. Coordinate units carry through unchanged: points measured in metres produce a distance in metres.

title: Circle Calculator
description: Derive a circle’s radius, diameter, circumference, and area from one known measurement. Select the input type so the calculator applies the correct relationship instead of treating a diameter as a radius. The circle relations are d=2r, circumference=2πr, and area=πr². If circumference or area is entered, radius is recovered before the other values are calculated.

title: Surface Area Calculator
description: Find the total outside area of a cube, rectangular box, sphere, cylinder, cone, or square pyramid. Enter the dimensions for the selected solid to distinguish lateral area from the full area including bases. The formulas include 6a² for a cube, 2(lw+lh+wh) for a box, 4πr² for a sphere, and 2πr²+2πrh for a closed cylinder. Cone and pyramid calculations use slant height.

title: Pythagorean Theorem Calculator
description: Solve a right triangle when two side lengths are known, identifying the hypotenuse when needed. The tool checks whether the supplied pair can form a right triangle and reports the missing side together with the verification relation. For legs a and b, c=√(a²+b²). If hypotenuse c and leg a are known, the remaining leg is √(c²−a²), requiring c>a. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle and is always the longest side; checking this ordering prevents taking the square root of a negative value.

title: Right Triangle Calculator
description: Complete a right triangle from two known measurements, such as two legs or a leg and an acute angle. The answer includes both acute angles and the hypotenuse, using degrees for angle inputs. The acute angles sum to 90°. Side ratios follow sine, cosine, and tangent; with legs a,b, hypotenuse c=√(a²+b²). In the side-angle mode, the given leg is treated as opposite the entered angle; the second leg and hypotenuse are derived from the trigonometric ratios.

title: Root Calculator
description: Find the principal nth root of a real number, including odd roots of negative values. The index must be a positive integer, and even roots of negative radicands are rejected because they are not real. The nth root r satisfies rⁿ=x. For even n, x must be nonnegative; for odd n, the real root keeps the sign of x. For an even index there are two signed solutions to rⁿ=x when x is positive, but the principal root returned here is the nonnegative one.

title: Least Common Multiple Calculator
description: Find the least common multiple of two positive integers, the smallest positive number divisible by both. The result is useful for aligning repeating cycles and finding a common denominator for whole-number fractions. For positive integers a and b, lcm(a,b)=a×b/gcd(a,b). Euclid’s algorithm finds the greatest common divisor efficiently.

title: Greatest Common Factor Calculator
description: Find the greatest common factor (greatest common divisor) shared by two integers. The result can reduce fractions, simplify ratios, or identify the largest equal grouping that divides both quantities evenly. Euclid’s algorithm repeatedly replaces (a,b) with (b,a mod b) until the remainder is zero; the last nonzero value is the greatest common factor.

title: Factor Calculator
description: List all positive factor pairs of a positive integer and identify its prime or composite status. Seeing the pairs gives a practical way to check divisibility and understand how the integer can be built from smaller whole numbers. A factor pair (d,n/d) is recorded whenever d divides n exactly. Trial divisors are checked only through √n, since larger partners have already appeared.

title: Rounding Calculator
description: Round a decimal number to a chosen number of decimal places or significant figures. The result follows the common half-up rule for magnitude, while preserving a clear indication of the selected precision. For decimal places, scale by 10^d, round the magnitude at the halfway point upward, then restore the sign. Significant-figure mode derives the decimal place from the value’s order of magnitude.

title: Matrix Calculator
description: Add, subtract, or multiply two small matrices and show the resulting matrix with compatible dimensions. This matrix calculator validates row lengths and multiplication shape before computing, so an invalid operation is explained rather than silently truncated. Addition and subtraction are element-wise and require equal dimensions. Multiplication uses Cᵢⱼ=ΣₖAᵢₖBₖⱼ, requiring columns of A to match rows of B. Matrix multiplication is order-sensitive, so reversing A and B can change both the dimensions and the result; the entered A×B order is preserved.

title: Scientific Notation Calculator
description: Convert a finite decimal to normalized scientific notation or turn a coefficient and exponent into its ordinary decimal value. Normalized notation keeps one nonzero digit before the decimal point and makes powers of ten easier to compare. A nonzero value is expressed as m×10^e where 1≤|m|<10. Conversion back multiplies the coefficient by 10^e. The exponent therefore records how many places the decimal point moves, making very large and very small magnitudes easier to read without changing the value.

title: Big Number Calculator
description: Add, subtract, multiply, or divide large whole numbers without losing integer precision to floating-point rounding. Inputs are parsed as decimal integers and results are returned exactly, subject to a practical digit limit. The operation uses arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic. Division reports quotient and remainder because two integers do not always divide evenly.

title: Prime Factorization Calculator
description: Express a positive integer as a product of prime powers and list the prime factors with multiplicity. The factorization is canonical, so it can also support divisor counting and simplification work. Repeatedly divide by the smallest candidate prime until it no longer divides the remaining value; continue until the remainder itself is prime. The fundamental theorem of arithmetic guarantees that every integer greater than 1 has one unique prime factorization apart from factor order.

title: Common Factor Calculator
description: List the positive common factors shared by two integers and show their greatest common factor. This makes the full shared divisor set visible instead of returning only the largest simplification factor. The shared factors are the positive divisors of gcd(|a|,|b|). Euclid’s algorithm finds the gcd, after which its divisor pairs enumerate the common set.

title: Basic Calculator
description: Evaluate a basic arithmetic expression with parentheses and standard precedence for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. The parser rejects unsupported characters and malformed expressions rather than executing arbitrary code. Multiplication and division are evaluated before addition and subtraction; parentheses override precedence. Unary signs and decimal literals are supported.

title: Long Division Calculator
description: Divide one signed integer by another and show the integer quotient, remainder, and decimal quotient. The remainder follows the dividend’s sign, matching truncation toward zero. For integers a and b≠0, quotient q=trunc(a/b) and remainder r=a−qb, so a=bq+r. This convention truncates the decimal quotient toward zero; some school methods instead use a nonnegative remainder, so the sign convention matters when either input is negative.

title: Average Calculator
description: Calculate the arithmetic average of a list of measurements and show the count and total used. The mean is a useful central summary when values are on the same scale and each observation should receive equal weight. Arithmetic mean = (x₁+x₂+…+xₙ)/n. Every entered value contributes once, regardless of its size. Because extreme observations pull the mean toward themselves, compare it with the median when the list is skewed or contains outliers.

title: P-value Calculator
description: Convert a z statistic to a left-tailed, right-tailed, or two-tailed normal-theory p-value. The output is a tail area under the standard normal distribution and must be interpreted with the test design and assumptions. For standard normal Z, left tail is Φ(z), right tail is 1−Φ(z), and two-tail is 2[1−Φ(|z|)]. A numerical approximation evaluates Φ. The p-value is conditional on the null model and chosen tail direction; it is neither the probability that the null is true nor a measure of effect size.

title: Age Calculator
description: Find a person’s completed age between two calendar dates. Calendar anniversaries are compared in UTC, so daylight-saving changes cannot add or remove a day. The result also reports elapsed days and the next birthday; a February 29 birthday is observed on March 1 in non-leap years.

title: Date Calculator
description: Add or subtract a signed number of calendar days from a chosen date. Calendar arithmetic is performed at midnight UTC and keeps the intended year-month-day even across daylight-saving transitions.

title: Time Calculator
description: Add or subtract clock durations using hours, minutes, and seconds. The output wraps across midnight and separately reports how many whole days the arithmetic crossed. Enter durations as elapsed time, not as local timestamps.

title: Hours Calculator
description: Convert a decimal hour total into hours and minutes, or convert hours and minutes back to decimal hours. The decimal result is useful for payroll and timesheets, while the split form avoids treating minutes as hundredths of an hour.

title: GPA Calculator
description: Compute a weighted grade-point average from course grades and credit weights. Enter one grade point per course and its credit value; total quality points are divided by total credits. This calculator does not assume a country’s grading scale, so translate grades to your institution’s scale first.

title: Grade Calculator
description: Calculate a course average from scores and their percentage weights, then estimate the score needed on a remaining assessment to reach a target. Weights should sum to 100% across completed and remaining work; if they do not, the weighted average is normalized over entered completed work.

title: Height Calculator
description: Convert height between centimeters, meters, feet, and inches without mixing decimal feet with feet-and-inches notation. The equivalent is calculated from exact unit ratios and rounded only for display.

title: Concrete Calculator
description: Estimate concrete volume for a rectangular slab using length, width, and thickness. The output includes cubic meters, cubic yards, and an optional overage allowance; it does not account for irregular edges, subgrade losses, or reinforcement displacement.

title: IP Subnet Calculator
description: Inspect an IPv4 address and CIDR prefix to determine its network, broadcast address, mask, and usable host range. This is arithmetic for conventional IPv4 subnets; /31 and /32 have special point-to-point and host semantics, which are identified in the result.

title: Bra Size Calculator
description: Estimate a US/UK-style band and cup size from underbust and bust measurements in inches. The result is a starting point because sizing systems, brands, fit preferences, and measurement technique differ; sister sizes can feel different across styles.

title: Password Generator
description: Generate a password from user-selected length and character groups using a cryptographically secure random source. Each enabled group is guaranteed to appear at least once, and rejection sampling avoids modulo bias. Keep generated secrets private and store them in a password manager.

title: Dice Roller
description: Simulate one or more fair dice with a chosen number of sides and report each roll plus the total. Secure runtime randomness is used when available; every face from 1 through the selected side count has equal probability.

title: Conversion Calculator
description: Convert between common length, mass, volume, temperature, area, speed, and energy units with explicit source and destination units. Conversions use fixed ratios or the standard affine temperature equations, so temperature offsets are not treated as simple multipliers.

title: Fuel Cost Calculator
description: Estimate trip fuel expense from distance, fuel economy, and the price per fuel unit. Choose metric consumption (L/100 km) or distance-per-volume (mpg or km/L); the calculator converts the required fuel amount before multiplying by price.

title: Voltage Drop Calculator
description: Estimate DC two-conductor cable voltage drop using conductor resistivity, length, and current. The round-trip length is twice the one-way run, and resistance scales with conductor area; this simplified model excludes connector resistance, temperature rise, AC reactance, and installation-code limits.

title: BTU Calculator
description: Estimate heating or cooling capacity in BTU per hour from room area and an adjustable load factor. The result is a screening estimate only; insulation, windows, ceiling height, climate, occupancy, and equipment efficiency can change a real load calculation substantially.

title: Square Footage Calculator
description: Find floor or surface area from length and width, with a choice of feet or meters and an optional count of identical rectangles. The calculator reports square feet and square meters; split complex spaces into rectangles and add their areas.

title: Time Card Calculator
description: Calculate elapsed paid time from clock-in and clock-out times, including an unpaid break and an overnight shift. Enter times in 24-hour format; if clock-out is earlier than clock-in, the shift is treated as ending the next day.

title: Time Zone Calculator
description: Convert a local date and time between two named IANA time zones using their daylight-saving rules for that date. Results retain the destination’s local clock and UTC offset, and flag invalid zones or nonexistent local times rather than silently guessing.

title: Love Calculator
description: Create a playful compatibility score from two names using a repeatable character-code calculation. It is entertainment only: names cannot measure relationship quality, consent, communication, or compatibility. Use the result as a lighthearted conversation starter, not advice.

title: GDP Calculator
description: Estimate gross domestic product with the expenditure identity: household consumption plus investment plus government purchases plus exports minus imports. Enter values in one consistent currency and time period; this computes a nominal total and does not adjust for inflation or population.

title: Gas Mileage Calculator
description: Calculate fuel economy from distance traveled and fuel consumed, showing both miles per US gallon and liters per 100 kilometers where applicable. Distance and fuel must be measured over the same fill-to-fill interval for a meaningful result.

title: Horsepower Calculator
description: Estimate mechanical horsepower from torque and rotational speed using HP = torque × RPM / 5252 when torque is in lb-ft. The result is shaft power under that conventional unit system; drivetrain losses and measurement accuracy are not included.

title: Engine Horsepower Calculator
description: Estimate engine power from torque and engine speed, with explicit choices for lb-ft or newton-meters and horsepower or kilowatts. Torque and RPM must refer to the same operating point; peak torque and peak RPM from different points cannot be combined into peak power.

title: Stair Calculator
description: Lay out a straight staircase from floor-to-floor rise and available horizontal run. It computes integer risers, actual riser height, approximate tread depth, and pitch; verify headroom, landing, handrail, and local building-code rules before building.

title: Resistor Calculator
description: Decode a four-band resistor color code into nominal resistance and tolerance, or calculate a series resistor for an LED from supply voltage, LED forward voltage, and target current. The current-limiting calculation is idealized; choose a standard value and check resistor power dissipation.

title: Ohms Law Calculator
description: Solve one unknown in Ohm’s law using any two of voltage, current, and resistance, then report power. Inputs must describe the same circuit condition; the equations model ideal lumped electrical behavior and do not cover nonlinear components or transient effects.

title: Electricity Calculator
description: Estimate electrical energy and cost from power, hours of use, and an adjustable price per kilowatt-hour. For variable loads, use average power over the measured interval; fixed charges, taxes, demand fees, and time-of-use rates are not included.

title: Shoe Size Conversion
description: Convert a shoe size between selected US men’s, US women’s, UK, and EU scales using a practical chart-based approximation. Manufacturers vary in last shape and labeling, so use the brand’s own chart and foot length for a purchase decision.

title: Tip Calculator
description: Calculate a restaurant tip from the bill and tip percentage, then split the total among diners. You can choose whether the percentage applies before or after tax; the per-person result is rounded for currency display, so the final person may need to absorb a cent difference.

title: Mileage Calculator
description: Compute distance between two odometer readings, optionally subtracting a correction or comparing multiple trips. Enter values in the same distance unit; this tool does not infer a route or account for GPS/odometer calibration.

title: Density Calculator
description: Calculate density as mass divided by volume and show the equivalent in common SI units. Mass and volume must describe the same sample at the same conditions; porous materials, mixtures, and temperature-sensitive fluids may need a more specific measurement method.

title: Mass Calculator
description: Find mass from density and volume using m = ρV, with matching unit choices and equivalent outputs in grams and kilograms. The estimate assumes density is uniform throughout the object and that the chosen density matches its material and conditions.

title: Weight Calculator
description: Convert mass to gravitational force using W = m × g, with an editable gravitational acceleration. The default is standard Earth gravity; this is a force estimate and should not be confused with everyday scale readings that often display mass units.

title: Speed Calculator
description: Calculate average speed from distance and elapsed time and convert between common speed units. Average speed uses total distance divided by total duration; it differs from average velocity when direction and displacement matter.

title: Molarity Calculator
description: Calculate solution molarity from solute amount and final solution volume, or determine the mass required when molecular weight is known. Volume must be final solution volume in liters, not simply solvent volume before dissolving.

title: Molecular Weight Calculator
description: Estimate molar mass by parsing a chemical formula and summing standard atomic weights for each element and subscript. Parentheses and nested groups are supported; charges, isotope notation, hydrates, and ambiguous informal names should be entered as explicit formulas or handled by a chemistry reference.

title: Roman Numeral Converter
description: Convert positive integers to standard Roman numerals or validate and parse a canonical Roman numeral. The supported range is 1 through 3,999, using subtractive forms such as IV and CM; historical variants and zero are not represented.

title: Golf Handicap Calculator
description: Estimate a World Handicap System index from 3 to 20 entered score differentials. It selects the lowest differentials, applies the published adjustment for 3, 4, and 6 scores, then rounds to one decimal place. The calculation assumes you already have valid differentials and omits soft caps, exceptional-score adjustments, and committee review, so it is not an official handicap record.

title: Sleep Calculator
description: Plan wake-up or bedtime windows around approximate 90-minute sleep cycles and a configurable time to fall asleep. Sleep cycles vary between people and across the night; the suggestions are planning estimates, not a diagnosis or a promise to wake refreshed.

title: Tire Size Calculator
description: Estimate tire sidewall height, overall diameter, circumference, and speedometer difference from a metric tire code such as 205/55R16. It assumes the nominal width and aspect ratio; actual dimensions vary by model, rim width, pressure, wear, and load.

title: Roofing Calculator
description: Estimate roof covering area from the building footprint, roof pitch, and waste allowance. The pitch multiplier converts horizontal plan area to sloped surface area; valleys, dormers, overhangs, and complex geometry may require a measured takeoff.

title: Tile Calculator
description: Estimate tile count from floor area and individual tile dimensions, with an adjustable cutting and breakage allowance. The calculation rounds up to whole tiles and excludes grout spacing, pattern cuts, spare stock, and carton pack sizes unless you account for them in the allowance.

title: Mulch Calculator
description: Estimate mulch volume from bed area and target depth, then convert cubic feet to cubic yards. Measure each bed and add its area; settling, uneven ground, and the product’s moisture content affect the delivered depth.

title: Gravel Calculator
description: Estimate gravel volume from area and compacted depth, with an editable material density to convert volume to mass. Aggregate density varies with grading, moisture, and compaction, so use supplier data for a reliable tonnage order.

title: Wind Chill Calculator
description: Estimate the US National Weather Service wind-chill temperature from air temperature in Fahrenheit and wind speed in miles per hour. The index applies only at or below 50°F with wind above 3 mph and assumes shade; sun exposure can change how conditions feel.

title: Heat Index Calculator
description: Estimate apparent heat using the National Weather Service Rothfusz regression for warm, humid conditions, with its low-humidity and high-humidity adjustments. It is intended for shaded conditions and can be misleading outside its calibrated range; direct sun and exertion increase heat stress.

title: Dew Point Calculator
description: Estimate dew point from air temperature and relative humidity with the Magnus approximation. The result represents the temperature at which air becomes saturated under the model; indoor surfaces, pressure, and measurement error can affect condensation in practice.

title: Bandwidth Calculator
description: Estimate transfer time or required data rate from file size and network speed, with decimal or binary byte units and an efficiency allowance. The ideal rate ignores latency, congestion, protocol overhead, server limits, and competing traffic; real transfers often take longer.

title: Base64 Encode Decode
description: Encode UTF-8 text as Base64 or decode Base64 back into text, validating malformed input instead of silently accepting corrupted data. Base64 is a text representation, not encryption; anyone who obtains the encoded string can decode it.

title: URL Encode Decode
description: Percent-encode or decode URL components as UTF-8 text. Component encoding treats spaces as %20 and preserves only unreserved characters; full URL structures should be assembled from separately encoded path and query components.

title: Time Duration Calculator
description: Find elapsed duration between two clock times, optionally spanning midnight, and return the total in hours and minutes. If end time is earlier than start, the calculator interprets it as the next day; use the date calculator for durations across multiple dates.

title: Day Counter
description: Count whole calendar-day boundaries between two dates and optionally use inclusive counting. Dates are compared in UTC so daylight-saving transitions do not change the day count. Reverse endpoints are accepted and reported as an absolute difference.

title: Day of the Week Calculator
description: Determine the weekday for a valid Gregorian calendar date and show its ISO weekday number. The date is validated before calculation, so impossible dates such as February 30 are rejected rather than normalized into March.

title: Unit Price Calculator
description: Compare package sizes on equal terms. See the price per unit for two options and how much you save by choosing the better value.

title: Reading Time Calculator
description: Estimate how long an article, essay or document will take to read. Adjust reading speed for your audience and compare a fast read with a careful one.

title: Break-Even Calculator
description: Find how many products you need to sell to cover fixed costs. Explore the relationship between price, variable cost and the contribution each sale makes.
